issues.description: The template's ArrayHelpers class defines a method named appendElement (ArrayHelpers.appendElement) but the template's Stock and other code call ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray. This name mismatch causes compilation errors for students working from the template. The solution repository and Stock implementation expect addElementToArray, while the template's ArrayHelpers uses a different name, making the template inconsistent and blocking students from compiling and following the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ArrayHelpers API consistent in the template. Rename the method appendElement to addElementToArray (keeping the same generic signature and behavior) so that calls from Stock and other classes compile, or alternatively change callers to use appendElement. Prefer renaming the template ArrayHelpers to addElementToArray to match the solution and existing usages in the template Stock.

issues.description: The helper method for appending elements to arrays has inconsistent identifiers: the template's ArrayHelpers defines appendElement(T[] array, T element) but other code (template Stock.java and the solution's ArrayHelpers) expect addElementToArray(T[] array, T element). This mismatch creates a cognitive mapping problem and a compile-time error, since students see different names for the same utility operation and may be unsure which to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across repositories. Rename the template method appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (or update all callers to use appendElement). Prefer changing template ArrayHelpers to addElementToArray to match Stock.java and the solution implementation.
